title: Resolving a category error: DHL[3,2] yields H_1 ≤ 6, not H_1 = 2
description: We show, assuming the Dickson–Hardy–Littlewood-type hypothesis DHL[3,2] (currently known only conditionally, under GEH), that infinitely many consecutive prime gaps are at most 6, i.e. H_1 ≤ 6. This note does not prove DHL[3,2] or the Twin Prime Conjecture. We also prove unconditionally that every consecutive prime gap after 3 − 2 is at least 2, so H_1 ≤ 3 is equivalent to H_1 = 2 (twin primes), and that the minimal diameter of an admissible 3-tuple is 6. A toy-predicate model shows DHL[2,2] cannot be derived from the combinatorial form of DHL[3,2] alone (not an independence result for the primes). The parity barrier is used only as an explicit hypothesis. All results are formalized in Lean 4 + Mathlib with no sorry and only Lean's standard axioms.
